location: England, Norfolk, Caistor St Edmund temple
description: A Romano-Celtic temple in a walled precinct, just north east of the Roman walled town. Evidence of internal tessellated flooring and altars, a monumental entrance to the temenos, a multi-room building to the north east, and possibly a circular building.
bibliography: Gregory, and Gurney. “Excavations at Thornham, Warham, Wighton and Caistor, Norfolk.” East Anglian Archaeology 30 (1986).
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Caistor St Edmund Temple (Norfolk).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
